evals.prompt: Review all current working-tree changes in this repository before I commit. Include staged, unstaged, and new files, follow AGENTS.md, and focus on bugs that could ship rather than style.
evals.expected_output: A read-only evidence-first review that establishes the repository baseline and full working-tree scope, traces changed behavior beyond the diff, reports only concrete findings, and ends with verification gaps and a verdict.
assertions: The review establishes repository guidance and distinguishes staged, unstaged, untracked, and unrelated pre-existing changes.
Changed behavior is traced through relevant callers, consumers, contracts, side effects, and tests rather than reviewing changed lines in isolation.
Every reported finding contains a precise location, reachable failure scenario, impact, focused remediation direction, and confidence.
Style preferences and theoretical risks are omitted or clearly separated from actionable defects.
The response remains read-only and ends with block, needs follow-up, or no actionable findings.

evals.prompt: 審查這個已驗證的小型重構。測試與行為皆未改變；若找不到真正的缺陷，請直接說明，不要憑空提出建議。
evals.expected_output: A concise review that checks the affected contract and evidence, explicitly reports no actionable findings when none qualify, and identifies only material verification limits.
assertions: The response does not manufacture a finding merely to make the review appear useful.
It verifies the claimed behavior-preserving boundary against the available diff, callers, and tests.
Cosmetic preferences, generic best practices, and speculative future risks are not reported as defects.
Any unavailable runtime path or missing evidence is listed as a verification gap rather than a confirmed issue.
The final verdict is no actionable findings when no concrete defect is supported.

evals.prompt: Perform a broad code review of an authentication redirect change. There is a suspicious user-controlled URL, but framework validation and an allowlist may make it safe. Determine whether this blocks the change.
evals.expected_output: A coordinated broad and security-focused review that loads security-code-review, traces attacker control through validation to the redirect sink, separates confirmed exploitability from needs-verification evidence, and avoids severity by keyword.
assertions: The response routes vulnerability analysis through security-code-review while code-review retains the cross-domain verdict.
It verifies source, sink, allowlist, framework protections, reachability, and deployment context before calling the redirect exploitable.
A medium-confidence suspicion is placed under needs verification rather than reported as a confirmed blocker.
Any confirmed finding explains attacker outcome, affected trust boundary, evidence path, impact, and confidence.
The verdict follows verified exploitability and impact instead of treating every security-related pattern as Critical.

evals.prompt: Review a React checkout diff that changes loading, retry, keyboard focus, responsive CSS, and stale-request handling. Include browser-facing regression risks and test gaps.
evals.expected_output: A unified review that loads frontend-code-review for UI-specific evidence, keeps code-review responsible for finding quality and the verdict, and distinguishes code-supported defects from behavior that requires browser verification.
assertions: The response loads or routes through frontend-code-review for state UX, accessibility, responsive, rendering, and browser behavior.
It examines loading, error, retry, cancellation, stale state, focus, keyboard, narrow viewport, and relevant business behavior.
Findings that depend on runtime layout or interaction require browser evidence or are disclosed as unverified.
Frontend findings return to the common evidence, severity, deduplication, and verdict contract.
Missing browser or E2E coverage is reported as a test gap unless a concrete regression is demonstrated.

evals.prompt: Review a zero-downtime database migration that renames a column while old and new application versions may run together. Check deploy order, existing rows, backfill, rollback, retries, and public API compatibility.
evals.expected_output: An evidence-first compatibility review that loads the relevant migration and API specialists, traces mixed-version producers and consumers, and reports concrete rollout or data failures with deployment-aware remediation.
assertions: The response loads the narrow database migration and API contract Skills needed by the changed surfaces.
It checks expand-and-contract order, mixed-version reads and writes, defaults, existing data, backfill, indexes, retries, and rollback.
Public API, schema, serialization, and deployment compatibility are traced through known producers and consumers.
A finding names the exact rollout sequence or data state that fails rather than stating that migrations are generally risky.
Unverified production scale or operational assumptions remain verification gaps and are not promoted into defects.

evals.expected_output: A bounded snippet review that analyzes what the supplied code proves, loads JavaScript guidance when useful, avoids invented repository context, and states which conclusions require callers or runtime evidence.
assertions: The response treats the pasted snippet as the full authorized scope and uses a supplied symbol, quoted expression, or clearly labeled snippet-relative location instead of inventing a repository path.
It distinguishes defects visible in the function from behavior that depends on callers, configuration, versions, or tests.
JavaScript async, cancellation, error, cleanup, and concurrency behavior is checked when relevant.
Speculative integration concerns are listed as questions or scope limitations instead of confirmed findings.
The output still uses concrete failure scenarios, impact, direction, confidence, and a clear verdict.

evals.prompt: Review GitHub pull request 42 using its commits, comments, changed files, and failing checks. Do not post anything to GitHub; just give me the findings and verdict.
evals.expected_output: A read-only PR review that loads github-code-review for exact GitHub context and code-review for evidence and verdict, without publishing comments or changing review state.
assertions: The response resolves the exact repository and PR and inspects base, head, merge-base diff, commits, comments, files, and checks.
GitHub context is used to understand intent and failures, while the common code-review contract governs findings and verdict.
The response does not post comments, approve, request changes, or mutate the pull request.
Failing checks are investigated and correlated with the changed behavior instead of merely repeated.
Findings remain precise, deduplicated, confidence-rated, and ordered by severity.

evals.prompt: A reviewer left six comments on my pull request. Validate each comment, reject false positives, implement the accepted fixes, and prepare evidence for re-review.
evals.expected_output: A route to receiving-code-review rather than an original independent review, with each incoming finding validated before remediation and implementation kept separate from reviewer ownership.
assertions: The response recognizes that findings already exist and routes ownership to receiving-code-review.
Each comment is validated against current code and requirements before being accepted, rejected, or deferred.
The original code-review role is not used to both author and independently approve its own fixes.
Accepted fixes require focused implementation and regression evidence before re-review.
The handoff preserves finding identity, resolution status, remaining uncertainty, and an independent re-review step.

evals.prompt: Review a change containing one small package manifest edit, a regenerated 20,000-line dependency artifact, and passing package tests. Decide the review depth from actual behavior and risk instead of diff size.
evals.expected_output: A proportionate review that identifies the manifest as canonical, treats generated output as derived evidence, and does not escalate the review merely because the mechanical diff is large.
assertions: The response classifies review depth from trust boundaries, contracts, reversibility, blast radius, and evidence rather than line count.
The generated artifact is traced to its canonical manifest or generator and is not reviewed line by line.
Packaging, dependency, compatibility, and reproducibility effects are checked where relevant.
Passing tests inform confidence but do not replace review of the changed package contract.
The coverage ledger marks the manifest as reviewed and the generated artifact as derived.

evals.prompt: Review a three-line change that removes an authorization guard from a public administrator endpoint. The author calls it cleanup, one reviewer says the framework already protects it, and another says it is a privilege escalation.
evals.expected_output: An elevated broad and security-focused review that verifies the current authorization path and negative evidence, resolves reviewer disagreement from code rather than votes, and blocks only if exploitability is confirmed.
assertions: The small diff is classified as elevated because it changes a public authorization boundary.
The response routes exploitability analysis through security-code-review and checks route, middleware, framework, resource ownership, and deployment protections.
Independent validation is used when available and permitted; otherwise the missing cross-validation is disclosed.
Reviewer agreement or disagreement does not determine severity or whether the finding survives.
The final finding is confirmed, rejected, or placed under needs verification from concrete reachability and impact evidence.

evals.prompt: Review a change that deletes input normalization which looks redundant. Current unit tests pass, but an earlier commit may have added it after a production compatibility incident. Use history only if it can clarify the invariant.
evals.expected_output: A selective history-assisted review that examines the relevant prior change and base-versus-head behavior without blanket blame or treating commit text as proof.
assertions: The response identifies safeguard removal and unclear intent as reasons for selective git history inspection.
Only relevant log, show, or blame context is inspected rather than blaming every changed line.
The earlier invariant and affected consumers are checked against current code and conditions.
Commit messages and authorship are treated as context that must be corroborated by behavior or tests.
A compatibility finding requires a concrete input, consumer, failure path, and current impact.

evals.prompt: Review a retry feature whose implementation passes its new tests but violates the acceptance requirement that payment submissions must never be duplicated after a timeout.
evals.expected_output: A two-pass elevated review that first detects the specification mismatch and then traces idempotency, retries, side effects, persistence, and tests to establish the implementation failure.
assertions: The intent and specification pass compares behavior with the explicit no-duplicate acceptance criterion before judging code quality.
The implementation-safety pass traces timeout, retry, idempotency key, persistence, and external side effects.
Passing tests do not override an authoritative acceptance criterion they fail to represent.
Any finding gives the exact timeout and retry sequence that creates a duplicate payment and its impact.
The review profile is elevated because value transfer, retries, and irreversible side effects are involved.

evals.prompt: Review a medium-sized cross-platform change spanning a shared API contract, generated clients, a web implementation, and an iOS binary behavior that cannot be run in this environment. Show exactly what the verdict covers.
evals.expected_output: A standard or elevated review with an honest behavior-surface coverage ledger that separates reviewed, derived, skipped, and unavailable evidence without claiming repository-wide completeness.
assertions: The shared contract and reachable source implementations are marked reviewed with concrete evidence.
Generated clients are marked derived and traced to their schema or generator.
Any intentionally excluded area is marked skipped with a scope reason rather than silently omitted.
The unavailable iOS runtime path is identified with its effect on confidence and verdict.
The response does not claim complete platform coverage beyond the frozen baseline and available evidence.

evals.prompt: Re-review GitHub pull request 42 after a new push. A prior finding was fixed, one was dismissed as a false positive, and a third appears to have returned under the same root cause. Do not post comments.
evals.expected_output: A read-only GitHub re-review that freezes the new head, preserves review-round and finding identity, verifies prior acceptance criteria, and avoids duplicate comments while reopening a genuinely regressed issue.
assertions: The response records repository, PR state, base SHA, new head SHA, merge base, and review-round identity.
Prior findings are classified as resolved, rejected, regressed, superseded, or unchanged against the current head.
Stable finding IDs are preserved when the root cause remains the same.
The dismissed finding is not repeated unless new evidence shows the current head still violates its acceptance criterion.
The response remains read-only and emits one deduplicated verdict without posting or changing GitHub state.
